title: Order edits failing
summary: A deploy of orders-service v2.15.0 at 13:31 UTC introduced a new order amendment endpoint. Starting at 13:33 UTC the service threw NullPointerExceptions in AmendOrderHandler.validate because order.limitPrice was null, causing 500 responses that propagated to edge-gateway. Error-rate metric spiked while CPU, memory, DB pool and latency stayed normal. No config, flag, secret or infra changes occurred in the window. Root cause is a code regression in the newly added handler.

hypothesis.mechanism: The new amendment handler validates limitPrice by calling compareTo without first checking for null; when a market order (limitPrice=null) is edited, a NullPointerException is thrown, resulting in a 500 that edge-gateway surfaces.
predictions: Rolling back to v2.14.3 or adding a null guard will eliminate the NPE and return error_rate to baseline

hypothesis.mechanism: A configuration change (e.g., feature flag) disabled a default price value causing limitPrice to be null.
predictions: A config change entry would appear in change history

hypothesis.mechanism: market-data-service started returning null prices, causing orders-service to store null limitPrice.
predictions: market-data-service logs would show errors or latency spikes

hypothesis.mechanism: Database connection pool saturation caused failures that manifest as NPE.
predictions: DB pool usage would approach max connections

facts.statement: orders-service v2.15.0 deployed (add order amendment endpoint) at 2026-10-05T13:31:20Z
orders-service logs show NullPointerException: order.limitPrice is null in AmendOrderHandler.validate (PATCH /v1/orders) – 413 occurrences, first at 13:33:01Z
edge-gateway logs show upstream orders-service returned 500 on /v1/orders – 379 occurrences, first at 13:34:05Z
orders-service error_rate metric rose from baseline 0.0021 to peak 0.0663 (mean 0.0185) between 13:31‑13:58Z
orders-service CPU, memory, DB pool usage, latency_p99 and RPS remained within normal bounds during the same window

assumptions.statement: Customer edit action maps to PATCH /v1/orders (the amendment endpoint added in v2.15.0)
assumptions.reason: Reported symptom is “changing price or quantity of an open order” and the new endpoint handles amendments

assumptions.statement: An order can legitimately have limitPrice == null (e.g., market orders) and the new validation omitted a null check
assumptions.reason: Exception shows direct dereference of limitPrice without guard; market orders lack a limit price

gaps.reason: Source code diffs are not accessible via available tooling

actions.description: Rollback orders-service to v2.14.3 or deploy hot‑fix adding null guard in AmendOrderHandler.validate
actions.rationale: Immediately stops the NPE and restores edit functionality

actions.description: Add defensive check `if (order.limitPrice == null) return errorResponse` before compareTo in the amendment handler
actions.rationale: Permanent code fix for the regression

actions.description: Add unit/integration test covering PATCH /v1/orders with missing limitPrice (market order)
actions.rationale: Prevents regression of same null‑check omission

actions.description: Update code‑review checklist to require null checks on optional fields for new endpoints
actions.rationale: Process improvement to catch similar bugs early

actions.description: Enable structured error code for “missing limit price” and add alert on its occurrence
